propositions: A committed uv lock freezes transitive dependencies, so any published advisory against a pinned version causes pip-audit to fail on all in-flight changes regardless of their code changes, blocking unrelated authors until the advisory is resolved.

Before the committed lock, upstream versions floated and advisories were picked up silently; after the lock, the gating job correctly finds real findings but with high response latency and no recheck path for real findings (job only retries DB-UNREACHABLE failures).

The distinction between override-dependencies (REPLACES requirement, correct for capping an upstream incompatibility) and constraint-dependencies (NARROWS constraint set, returns UNSATISFIABLE as expected output, not proof of impossibility) was not documented, leading to failed diagnosis and wrong remedies.

uv lock --upgrade-package is a no-op against an upstream cap from another dependency; overriding an upstream cap requires evidence that the incompatibility was fixed, and must carry a REMOVE-WHEN condition or outlive its justification silently.

The CI response posture must split by lane: verify lane blocks only if the change touches the dependency map (uv.lock / pyproject declarations); scheduled main lane fails on CRITICAL/HIGH advisories and routes to an owner for triage; releases are blocked by outstanding advisories.

Documentation must clarify the severity bar (CRITICAL and HIGH fail, MEDIUM warns, LOW tracked), require explicit justification for override-dependencies, and surface the runbook and recheck limitations from the pip-audit job's own failure message.
